Hi Rafael / Kimberly,

Thanks for the draft Exhibit A — quick procurement question as we prepare the PO. Two items blocking internal approval:

1) Invoicing entity / tax residency: who should we route invoices to for tax purposes? Our accounting team is asking if Redwood will invoice Cloudline, Inc (US) or Cloudline Ltd (UK/EU). We can share a VAT registration if needed — attaching our tax cert.

2) Payment terms: procurement prefers Net 45 for new vendors; our legal is okay with Net 30 if we can get a staged commit schedule (so they can align the payments to budget windows). Can you confirm what Redwood is willing to accept?

Can you also confirm whether the redlines in Exhibit A (pricing ladder + min commit phasing) are the version you intend to send to legal? We attached the certificate to this message.

Thanks — small ask: can we get a single-line summary of final invoice entity + payment term so I can trigger the PO?

Best,

Cloudline Health

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick note and for the tax cert. Appreciate the context.

Short answers up front:
- Invoice entity: Redwood recommends invoicing Cloudline, Inc (US) to match the commercial contract; if Cloudline prefers the EU entity for VAT reasons we can accommodate but will need the EU VAT id and a billing contact (to handle reverse-charge mechanics).
- Payment terms: Standard is Net 30. We can agree to a staged commit schedule so Cloudline has payment phasing aligned to budget windows. Proposed split: 60% at activation (covers initial reserve capacity), then 40% billed in equal quarterly tranches over the first 12 months.

I've attached ExhibitA_draft_v3_redlines.docx — this includes the pricing ladder and a suggested clause that handles tax responsibility (short form). If Cloudline will require Net 45, we can accept Net 45 for the first invoice only (one-time exception) but prefer Net 30 as standard for forecasting and cash management.

Next steps I suggest:
- Kimberly to confirm Finance is OK with staged invoice milestones and the 60/40 split.
- Priya to confirm preferred invoicing entity and share VAT/registration if EU.
- Ben / Laura — can Legal review the tax indemnity language in Exhibit A (attached) and advise if it's sufficient to avoid withholding exposure?

If that works I can update the order form and send for signature (DocuSign).

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference

Attachment: ExhibitA_draft_v3_redlines.docx
